abstract: Degeneration of dopamine (DA) neurons and reduced DA levels in the brain is recognized as an underlying cause of Parkinson's Disease (PD). Levodopa (L-DOPA) is the standard treatment, but its effectiveness wanes over time and prolonged use can cause L-DOPA-induced dyskinesia (LID). AAV-mediated aromatic L-amino acid decarboxylase (AADC) expression in the striatum combined with L-DOPA shows promise for symptomatic improvement but requires invasive delivery. Here, we generate enhancer-driven AAVs to drive AADC expression in key cell types and pair them with a blood-brain barrier (BBB)-penetrant capsid. Across two delivery routes and PD mouse models, cell type-specific AADC expression improves survival and ameliorates motor deficits and LID, with similar or greater phenotypic rescue than ubiquitous AADC expression. We further demonstrate the conservation of enhancer-driven AADC specificity in non-human primates (NHP). This viral strategy, combined with L-DOPA, may enable a less invasive and better tolerated approach to alleviate PD motor deficits.
